Indian Standard (Reaffirmed 1997) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
RONGEUR, PITUITARY 



1. Scope— Dimensional and other requirements for pituitary rongeur used in neurosurgery. 

2. Type, Shape and Dimensions 

2.1 The pituitary rongeur shall be of the following two types: 

Type 1 — Straight, up-bite or down-bite jaws; and 
Type 2 — Angled up-bite or down-bite jaws. 

2.2 The shape and dimensions shall be as shown in Fig. 1 unless otherwise agreed to between 

the purchaser and the supplier. 

2.3 The dimensions shall be as given in Table 1.

2.3.1 A deviation of ±2*5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

2.3.2 A deviation of ± 2° shall be allowed for angular dimensions. 

3. Material 

3.1 Arms and Jaws — Stainless steel conforming to designation 4CCr13 of IS : 6603-1972 * Specifica- 
tion for stainless steel bars and flats'. 

3.2 Rivets — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 12CM3 of IS : 6528-1972 ' Specification for 
stainless steel wire \ 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The rongeur shall be free from scale, burrs, cracks, pits, tool marks and other surface defects. 

4.2 All edges shall be smoothly rounded off except the cutting edge, which shall be as shown in 
Fig, 1. 

4.3 The rongeur shall operate smoothly and there shall be no play between the fixed jaw and the 
movable jaw. The opening and closing action shall be neither too hard nor too slack. On closure, 
the jaws shall register precisely. 

4.4 A hole of 1 mm diameter shall be provided in the centre of the fixed jaw to allow overflow of the 
entrapped fluid. If required by the purchasers similar hole may be provided in the other jaw as well. 



4.5 The rongeur shall be finished bright and passivated.

5. Heat Treatment — The rongeur shall be uniformly hardened and tempered to a hardness of 540 
to 600 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 The rongeur shall be made to bite off a piese of chamois leather of 1 mm thickness. The rongeur 
shall do it easily and cleanly. This shall be repeated 10 times. During and on completion of the 
test, the rongeur shall show no sign of damage. 

6.2 Corrosion Resistance — The rongeur shall be tested in accordance with IS : 7531-1975 ' Method 
for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments \ 
There shall be no sign of corrosion and the rongeur shall operate smoothly after the test. 

7. Marking— The rongeur shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, 
initials or registered trade-mark and the word ■ stainless \ 

7.1 ISl Certification Marking— Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The rongeur shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper and then packed individually 
in cardboard carton. Alternatively, packing may be done as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier.
